priority_semantics: Repair priority, not CVSS or a claim of deployed exploitation. Reachability and default-disabled conditions are stated per finding.

methodology.review: Defensive static source review, caller tracing, specification comparison and existing-test inspection.
limitations: Static confidence concerns source-level defects, not demonstrated exploitation.
Lower-layer passing tests do not reproduce higher-journey failures.
The local import commit is not the upstream candidate identity.
LOCALPROOF and dormant paths are not approved production integrations.

findings.title: Payment-guidance cutoff blocks seller release before actual escrow expiry

static_confidence.basis: Signing-review, controller and screen gates require payment coordination, which blocks at 900 seconds remaining, while the canonical contract and G18 allow release before actual expiry.

scope.reachability: Explicitly constructed LOCALPROOF journey with a funded trade inside the final 900 seconds before expiry.
scope.default_app: No enabled production trading path established; default trading remains disabled.

evidence.observation: reviewActionReady permits release signing review only in payment-coordination.
Release requires payment-coordination and a fresh allow-guidance result.
The payment buffer is 900 seconds.
Remaining time at or below the buffer produces a blocked near-expiry decision.
Release visibility and local phase depend on fresh payment coordination.
Release request and signing confirmation reject stale guidance.
Seller release remains valid strictly before the actual deadline.

caller_chain: Screen requests release signing review.
reviewActionReady requires payment-coordination.
Confirmed release rereads the payment-guidance gate.
The 900-second payment buffer rejects otherwise valid seller release.

impact.description: A willing seller cannot complete release through this journey during the final 15 minutes, including after fiat has arrived.
preconditions: Trade is funded and not expired.
limits: Client-side LOCALPROOF obstruction, not a contract authorization bypass.
Original contract deadline and refund destination remain intact.
Independent recovery tooling exists.

remedy: Separate release eligibility from the gate for displaying payment instructions.
Update reviewActionReady, controller action checks, screen visibility and signing confirmation together.
Preserve seller fiat attestation, exact original binding, signing review and fresh funded-state/deployment/account/deadline checks.
Keep actionable payment instructions hidden inside the buffer; never settle automatically.
safe_regression_acceptance: Guidance allowed at 901 seconds, hidden at 900 and 899 seconds.
Explicit seller release remains possible after independent fresh preflight strictly before expiry.
At actual expiry release is refused and original refund rules remain available.
UI, signing review and controller agree on these boundaries.

coverage.method: Static trace and exact-candidate G18 comparison; no browser/transaction reproduction.
coverage.gap: Payment-buffer tests do not establish independent journey release eligibility.

references.support: Guidance stops at <=900 seconds; release may continue before expiry by independent preflight, and recovery information remains accessible.

findings.title: Proven transaction-send denial leaves the journey in reconciliation without a retry state

static_confidence.basis: The lifecycle records 4001 as a live verified no-hash failure, but the journey retains a reconciliation phase and requests native evidence for an unsent transaction.

components: LOCALPROOF approval, funding, release and refund
scope.reachability: Configured provider rejects eth_sendTransaction with code 4001 and local cancellation is successfully recorded.
scope.default_app: No enabled default production trading path.
scope.change_status: Candidate integration defect; separate from active prepared/unsent approval recovery work.

evidence.observation: 4001 records failed with no hash and live terminal verification, returning USER_REJECTED.
Failed maps to non-finalized reverted reconciliation outcome.
Lifecycle reconcile recognizes a live verified no-hash cancellation without chain transaction evidence.
Approval/funding retain approval-reconcile or reconcile on submission refusal.
Release/refund enter settling before submit and retain it on refusal.
Journey calls journal.reconcileNative first and leaves phase unchanged for non-finalized outcomes.
reconcileNative always invokes native observation without a live-terminal shortcut.
No-hash intent triggers transaction search, failing when no transaction exists.

caller_chain: Submission returns a proven USER_REJECTED cancellation.
Journey remains in transaction reconciliation.
Reconciliation requests native transaction discovery before consulting local cancellation proof.
No transaction is found; ordinary explicit preparation remains unavailable.

impact.description: Ordinary transaction-send denial prevents returning to normal explicit preparation in the current journey; release/refund denial obstructs another exit attempt from a funded trade.
preconditions: Lifecycle successfully persists and verifies local cancellation.
limits: Applies to transaction-send denial, not every wallet prompt.
Initial terms-signing denial has a separate communicationAccepted recovery path.
No lost principal, automatic resend or permanent on-chain lock demonstrated.
A persisted failed label alone must not authorize retry after restoration.

remedy: Introduce an explicit journey transition for cancellation established by the live lifecycle.
Return to the appropriate explicit approval/funding/exit review state with original trade and consent requirements.
Handle the non-finalized local terminal result explicitly; merely reordering reconciliation calls is insufficient because current journey logic only advances on finalized.
Keep unknown broadcasts, timeouts, response loss and restored terminal labels on conservative reconciliation paths.
Never automatically resubmit.
safe_regression_acceptance: 4001 denial for approval, funding, release and refund yields an explicit retry/review state without automatic resend.
Retry uses live cancellation proof and fresh action review.
Initial terms-signing refusal retains its separate recovery behavior.
Unknown broadcast outcomes and restored failed labels cannot take the proven-cancellation shortcut.
Lock, wallet changes and delayed results cannot revive retired submission capability.

coverage.method: Static end-to-end trace; no higher-journey reproduction.
coverage.existing_test: Contracts reviewer ran the unchanged lower-layer test in packages/domain/test/tx-lifecycle.test.mjs named 'reads retry through read-retry; sends never retry; rejection and integrity failures'; it passed.
coverage.gap: That lower-layer test does not verify journey phase recovery.

references.support: 4001 denotes user rejection; the project lifecycle supplies the local cancellation classification.

findings.title: Terminal journey receipts omit deferred payout credit and its recovery route
findings.classification: Conditional payout-status and recovery integration gap

static_confidence.basis: Canonical settlement can be terminal while recipient credit remains owed; journey receipt fields and controls contain no pending-credit observation or withdrawal recovery.

scope.reachability: Conditional on a canonical push payout failing and creating pending credit. Current fixture uses development EOAs and plain MockERC20; deferred payout is not demonstrated ordinary fixture behavior.
scope.default_app: No enabled default production trading path.
scope.change_status: Candidate journey completion gap; contract withdrawal and ABI helpers already exist.

evidence.observation: Release/refund set terminal state and then attempt payout.
Failed push records pending recipient/asset credit and emits PayoutDeferred.
Anyone may call withdraw, which pays only the credited recipient and preserves credit if it reverts.
Clients must surface PayoutDeferred and pending balance.
Terminal reconciliation creates transaction/state/fee receipt without pending-credit read.
Receipt/snapshot lacks deferred-credit or withdrawal-status fields.
Presentation accurately labels Escrow outcome but omits outstanding payout status.
No withdrawal or direct payout recovery action.
Pending-credit read and withdrawal builders already exist.
Fixture deploys canonical BasicEscrow with plain MockERC20 and development accounts.

caller_chain: Canonical settlement reaches Released/Refunded.
A failed push may create pending credit.
Journey enters receipt based on terminal escrow state.
No credit status or explicit recovery route appears.

impact.description: An affected user is not shown that asset delivery remains outstanding or a second recovery transaction may be required.
preconditions: Settlement succeeds but push payout fails for the bound recipient/asset.
User relies on journey receipt/recovery controls.
limits: Escrow disposition displayed is accurate; no explicit false claim of completed delivery.
No missing contract withdrawal, redirection flaw or live payout failure claimed.
Credit is aggregate per recipient/asset, not inherently attributable to one trade.
Permanently rejecting recipients or restricted assets may still prevent withdrawal.

remedy: Show escrow disposition separately from payout/credit status.
Read pending credit using verified canonical evidence and original recipient/asset binding.
Expose explicit recovery information or reviewed withdrawal using existing ABI/recovery support.
Explain aggregate credit semantics and retain evidence until payout closure.
Preserve fixed destination and never infer fiat verification.
safe_regression_acceptance: Normal completed payout shows zero owed.
Existing deferred-credit fixture shows correct credited recipient, asset, amount and recovery route.
Aggregate credit is not all attributed to one trade without evidence.
Withdrawal status changes only after fresh canonical evidence.
Retention protection remains until payout closure.

coverage.method: Static missing-field/call/control review; no failure induced.
coverage.gap: Contract support is not wired into journey receipt/recovery.

references.support: Terminal disposition can coexist with deferred credit; clients must show it.

findings.title: Pool-wide relay deduplication drops events needed by independent subscriptions
findings.classification: Subscription delivery and discovery availability defect

static_confidence.basis: One global event-ID cache suppresses later subscriber delivery; native observers have overlapping deletion filters and independent order books.

scope.reachability: Independent overlapping consumers share a RelayPool, or a new consumer requests history already delivered to an earlier one. Native context composition supplies a concrete caller.
scope.default_app: No default-app observer composition found; hints remain discovery-only.
scope.change_status: Inherited from main e9b9db3bfe9fd8ceb54f1eeebf481d82fd7a93aa; same global cache/check/one-handler pattern confirmed there.

evidence.observation: Global seenIds map is separate from subscription records.
Only event ID is remembered.
Seen events are dropped; new verified events are remembered and sent only to the frame's subscriber.
Closing one subscriber leaves shared history intact.
New subscriptions share suppression and receive no cached replay.
Each observer has an independent OrderBook.
Each order requests all deletions by its maker, then ignores another order's deletion inside its handler.

caller_chain: Order A and B observers share pool/maker.
B's valid deletion first arrives under A's broad deletion filter.
Pool remembers ID; A discards unrelated order event.
B's subsequent matching delivery is suppressed.

impact.description: Independent consumers miss verified ads/deletions/history and can retain stale discovery context until expiry or become unknown.
preconditions: Overlapping logical subscriptions or reused history request.
For the concrete deletion case, distinct order observers share a maker.
limits: Desired same-subscription multi-relay/reconnect deduplication is a different policy.
Read-only discovery context cannot authorize funding or settlement.
No malicious payload or exploit reproduction claimed.

remedy: Separate signature-validation caching from subscriber delivery accounting.
Track delivery per logical subscription/event, or verify once and dispatch to all matching consumers.
Allow new subscription lifetimes to retrieve requested history.
Preserve bounded memory and same-subscriber duplicate suppression.
safe_regression_acceptance: Two ordinary overlapping consumers each receive one event copy.
Distinct orders from the same maker receive their relevant deletions.
Recreated consumer receives requested retained history.
Existing one-subscriber multi-relay/reconnect expectations remain.
All caches remain bounded.

coverage.method: Static source trace and main comparison.
existing_tests: packages/relay/test/pool.test.mjs:69-82 overlapping filters, request-bound assertions only
coverage.gap: No inspected independent overlapping-consumer delivery assertion.

references.support: Independent subscriptions receive matching events under their subscription identifiers until closed.

findings.title: HTTP readers compare decoded Fetch bytes with encoded Content-Length

static_confidence.basis: Both readers count decoded Fetch stream bytes and require equality with a header that can describe encoded response bytes.

scope.reachability: Fetch-compatible port returns content-encoded data with visible Content-Length different from decoded size. No shipped generic-driver consumer found; configured updater and browser fixture use the update reader.
scope.default_app: Generic consumer absent and default update trust unconfigured.
scope.change_status: Generic driver identical to main; update reader repeats same defect. Combined as one finding.

evidence.observation: Fetch stream bytes counted and required to equal Content-Length.
Update reader repeats declared-length versus decoded-body equality.
Configured controller constructs update reader.
Locator, manifest, envelope and artifact reads use that reader.
Unconfigured trust/capabilities leave update authority unavailable.

caller_chain: Pinned HTTP request uses Fetch.
Fetch decodes Content-Encoding.
Reader totals decoded chunks.
Encoded Content-Length differs and valid response becomes ROUTE_UNAVAILABLE.

impact.description: Normally compressed JSON, manifests or assets can be refused despite valid authenticated decoded content.
preconditions: Response is content-encoded and exposes differing Content-Length.
limits: No signature bypass, vault compromise or automatic fallback established.
Custom normalized ports need their own explicit length contract.
Decoded-byte size caps must remain.

remedy: Make actual decoded stream length the authoritative content/memory bound.
Remove unconditional Content-Length equality or apply it only with positively established identity encoding or a documented normalized port contract.
Do not treat missing exposed Content-Encoding alone as proof of identity encoding under browser/CORS semantics.
Preserve stream error handling, pinned URL, no redirects/credentials, cancellation, physical drain and downstream signature/hash checks.
safe_regression_acceptance: Valid identity, gzip and Brotli responses yield intended decoded bytes.
Oversized decoded bodies still fail.
Errored streams remain failures.
Authenticated checks use intended decoded content.
No fallback or automatic retry introduced.

coverage.method: Static review plus primary Fetch standard; no compressed-response reproduction.
coverage.gap: Inspected tests do not model native Fetch decoding semantics.

references.support: Content encoding is handled before body exposure; the standard explicitly notes Content-Length unreliability after decoding.

findings.title: Transient relay failure leaves LOCALPROOF negotiation without a safe resume path

static_confidence.basis: Ad/exchange state commits before transport completion; outgoing signed events are local variables and retries repeat already-committed transitions.

scope.reachability: Isolated two-party journey after local preparation but before native funding, when publication or receipt fails.
scope.change_status: Candidate journey integration defect; exchange commit-after-signing contract is intentional.

evidence.observation: Delivery can fail on publish/pull/wrap receipt without retaining a pending-send record.
Seller ingests ad before publish and permits only accepted ingestion; take/offer commit before delivery and phase changes after success.
Acceptance commits before delivery; communicationAccepted is set only after peer success.
Offer/accept errors provide no resume transition.
Live previous take rejects repetition; take commits before returning its message.
Offer state commits before returned message.
Accept requires offered state and commits accepted before returned message.

caller_chain: Journey ingests ad or obtains signed SentMessage.
Local communication state is committed.
Subsequent delivery fails while visible phase stays wallet/review.
Retry re-ingests same/conflicting ad or repeats take/offer/accept, hitting duplicate/conflict/OUT_OF_ORDER.

impact.description: Ordinary transient relay failure can strand the current negotiation until controller reset, without in-place resend/resume.
limits: No production funds-loss claim.
Commit before uncertain delivery is intentional; missing delivery retention/resumption is the defect.
Separate from wallet transaction-send refusal.

remedy: Retain exact signed ad/message as owned pending delivery.
Separate communication state from transport outcome.
Provide deliberate same-event resend/resume and reconcile potentially applied peer result.
Do not silently roll back or regenerate possibly delivered signed content.
Clear pending private material on retirement.
safe_regression_acceptance: Ordinary transport failures at send/receive boundaries yield explicit resume state.
Retry reuses original identity and advances both parties once.
Delayed successful delivery does not duplicate transitions.
Existing exact-review/signature/native funding gates remain.
Lock/dispose clears pending bytes and suppresses late completion.

coverage.method: Static state trace; no relay fault reproduction.
existing_tests: Integrated journey uses serialized owned parties
coverage.gap: No inspected post-commit delivery-failure resumption coverage.

references.support: Explicit identical-event republish differs from automatic new-event retries; acknowledgment does not prove peer delivery.

findings.title: Failed accepted-release database opening stays cached for the store lifetime

static_confidence.basis: The rejected native-opening promise remains assigned and every later storage operation returns it.

scope.reachability: Explicitly constructed reused store suffers a native open failure, underlying condition clears, and same instance is retried.
scope.default_app: No default instance; actual browser fixture uses the real store.
scope.change_status: Confirmed in candidate; no introduction-versus-inheritance claim.

evidence.observation: Cached opening promise is never cleared after rejection.
Each operation awaits cached opening.
read/advance reuse store; explicit close is terminal.
Checking reads accepted store.
Acceptance rereads/advances supplied store.
Browser fixture constructs real store instances.
Existing fixture exercises native read/CAS and malformed stored data.

caller_chain: Controller calls store.
Initial native open rejects and stays cached.
Later operation reuses rejected promise.
No fresh opening occurs despite recovered storage condition.

impact.description: A transient storage failure disables checking/acceptance for that store instance until the store is recreated.
preconditions: Native attempt fails after promise caching.
limits: Controller recreation with the same store does not help.
No rollback-floor deletion or rollback bypass.
Early missing-factory/insecure-context refusal before caching is outside this condition.
Conditional low-priority reliability issue.

remedy: Clear cached promise on failure only if it still identifies that attempt.
Keep late-success closure so stale requests cannot install handles.
Keep explicit close terminal.
Reuse guarded failure-reset pattern from encrypted vault store.
safe_regression_acceptance: Initial native open failure then success permits later read on same store.
Old late completion cannot overwrite or clear newer attempt.
Explicit close remains terminal.
Rollback metadata is preserved.

coverage.method: Static cached-promise review; no failure reproduction.
coverage.existing_coverage: Native IndexedDB browser fixture exists; controller unit tests inject stores.
coverage.gap: Missing failed-open followed by retry on same store, not all native-store tests.

findings.title: Courier route-field authorization accepts incomplete selected-policy consent

Opaque evidence confirms a proper subset.
